title: What Does the Bible Say About Eating Pork? 26 Verses
description: Can Christians eat pork? What Leviticus forbids, what Jesus and Peter's vision changed, and what Paul says about food, with 26 verses.
keywords: what does the bible say about eating pork
clean and unclean animals in the bible
summary: The law of Moses forbade Israel to eat pork. Leviticus 11:7-8 and Deuteronomy 14:8 call the pig unclean, and the World English Bible uses the word pig in 18 verses while the King James Version says swine in 19. The word pork itself appears in neither. The New Testament changes the rule for believers: Mark 7:18-19 has Jesus teaching that food cannot defile a person and draws the conclusion that all foods are clean, Peter's vision in Acts 10:15 says not to call unclean what God has made clean, and Paul tells the Romans that nothing is unclean in itself (Romans 14:14) and the Corinthians to eat what is set before them (1 Corinthians 10:27). Most Christians therefore eat pork, while some, including Seventh-day Adventists and Messianic Jews, keep the Old Testament food laws. The verses below show the law and what changed.

faqs.a: Most Christians believe so. Jesus taught that food cannot defile a person, and Mark draws the conclusion that all foods are clean (Mark 7:18-19), Peter was told three times in a vision to kill and eat animals he had always considered unclean (Acts 10:9-16), and Paul writes that nothing is unclean in itself (Romans 14:14) and that food will not commend us to God (1 Corinthians 8:8). The early church council in Acts 15 kept only four requirements for Gentiles, and pork was not among them.

faqs.q: Why did God forbid pork in the Old Testament?
faqs.a: Leviticus 11:7 simply states that the pig is unclean because it divides the hoof but does not chew the cud. The Bible gives the broader purpose in Leviticus 11:44-45: to be holy, because God is holy, and to set Israel apart from the nations. Writers have also suggested health reasons, but the text does not say that.

faqs.q: Why do some Christians still avoid pork?
faqs.a: Some groups, among them Seventh-day Adventists and many Messianic Jews, read Jesus' words in Matthew 5:17 about not abolishing the law as keeping the Old Testament food laws in force. Most other Christians read Mark 7:18-19, Acts 10 and Romans 14 as ending those restrictions for believers. Paul says each believer should be fully convinced in his own mind (Romans 14:5) and not despise those who differ.

faqs.q: What did Jesus say about unclean food?
faqs.a: He said that nothing going into a person from outside can defile him, because food goes into the stomach, not the heart (Mark 7:18-19). Mark's account draws the conclusion that this makes all foods clean. In Matthew 15:11 he says what comes out of the mouth defiles a person.
